Based on my search, I can answer your question. "New York, New York" refers to **New York City, New York**, which is a unique case in U.S. administrative divisions.

New York City is composed of **five boroughs**, and each borough corresponds to a **county** (郡). However, unlike most places in the U.S. where counties contain cities, in New York City, the **five counties are subordinate to the city** rather than the other way around.

The five counties/boroughs are:

| Borough | County |
|---------|--------|
| Manhattan | **New York County** |
| Brooklyn | Kings County |
| Queens | Queens County |
| The Bronx | Bronx County |
| Staten Island | Richmond County |

So when people say "New York, New York," they typically mean **Manhattan**, which is **New York County**. The address "New York, NY" commonly refers to Manhattan specifically, though it can refer to the entire city.

This is a unique arrangement in the United States where the city level is higher than the county level, which is the opposite of how administrative divisions typically work elsewhere in the country.
